::: {#exr-miller-deriv-generalized-power-rule}
#### Generalized power rule

Find the derivative of

$$f(x) = \sqrt[3]{(5x - 2)^2} = (5x - 2)^{2/3}$$

for $x \ne 2/5$.
:::

::: {#sol-miller-deriv-generalized-power-rule}
Apply the generalized power rule $\dif{}{x}[g(x)]^r = r[g(x)]^{r-1}g'(x)$ with $g(x) = 5x - 2$ and $r = 2/3$:

$$f'(x) = \frac{2}{3}(5x - 2)^{2/3 - 1} \cd 5 = \frac{10}{3}(5x - 2)^{-1/3} = \frac{10}{3(5x - 2)^{1/3}}$$

*Remark:* Omitting the inner derivative $g'(x) = 5$ is a frequent mistake when applying the generalized power rule.
:::
